analysis:
The only changed hunk is in SSDPrefixCache.swift (head lines 1770-1778, evictOldestEntry). The old inline loop over index.oldestEntries() is replaced by a call to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:) with a closure. The closure still builds the URL via SSDBlockStore.fileURL(root:tag16Hex:) with an HMAC-derived tag, then calls retireIndexedEntries([url]). That function still takes removalLock and checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot before SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove. The guard hasSafeRoot at the top of evictOldestEntry is retained, and the evictions stat is still incremented only when freed > 0. Lines 691-1256 (donate, appendWindowSidecars) and 1257-1837 (stage, readWindowSidecars, staging tickets) are unchanged context. I saw nothing in them that regresses the T-041 posture: HMAC lookup tags, salt folding, per-donation floor, endurance pre-check, and metadata bindings (weightHash, layoutEpoch, lookupTag, window binding) all appear intact.

Open question: the implementation of SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest is not in the supplied evidence. The base code had specific behavior: it iterated the bounded snapshot, skipped valid-but-undeletable victims so a newer victim could satisfy the budget, and returned 0 on externalChange. I cannot verify the helper preserves these. If it does not, the consequence is disk-budget enforcement weakening, which is an availability and retention concern (the box-wide LRU budget in the T-041 mitigations). That is unverified and not evidence of a regression. The next pass should check the helper for bounded iteration, skipping of undeletable entries, externalChange handling, and that it never deletes outside config.root without the safe-path checks. Also confirm that the other callers of retireIndexedEntries are unaffected.
